key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual or after physical activity, coughing, or trauma. LOCATION: ANTERIOR CHEST WALL, costochondral junctions (where ribs meet cartilage), often left-sided. DURATION: Days to weeks. CHARACTER: SHARP, stabbing, localized. AGGRAVATING: Deep breathing, coughing, palpation of affected area, arm movements, twisting. RELIEVING: Rest, NSAIDs, avoiding movements. TIMING: Intermittent, worse with movements. SEVERITY: 4-7/10. KEY POSITIVES: REPRODUCIBLE with palpation (tender to touch), young patient, recent URI or cough, musculoskeletal pattern. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT radiating to arm/jaw, NOT exertional, NOT diaphoresis, NOT dyspnea.

red_flags: Radiation to arm or jaw (suggests cardiac)
